title: 1:1 deep-dive — routing, KV cache, capacity handoffs
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with Kiran (eng lead). Goal is to align on three concrete decisions we need this sprint: routing policy for low-latency vs low-cost tenants, KV/prefix cache rollout plan for Dedicated, and an owner for Private handoff doc set.

Current state (short):
- Routing: we have two candidate policies: latency-first (pin to nvlink pools) and cost-first (fallback to quantized small variants). SLI math shows latency-first improves p95 by ~110ms for chat workloads but increases per-token cost by ~0.9c on average (see INF-1278).
- KV cache: prototype landed in runtime PR (runtime#482) but only enabled for hosted models; Dedicated config not exposed in console yet. Early tests show 12–18% token reduction on prompt-heavy call traces. Needs autoscaling story.
- Private: multiple customers asking for an ops checklist (networking + KMS + audit) to cut onboarding time; no single doc owner.

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick sync (5m) — state check and any hot blockers.
2) Routing policy decision framework (10m) — agree on experiment to run next week (A/B or per-tenant rollout), success metrics, and who will instrument.
3) KV cache rollout plan (10m) — decide console knobs, default behavior for Dedicated, and autoscale considerations.
4) Handoff doc + owner for Private onboarding (5m) — assign owner and deadline.

Key questions I want answered by end of meeting:
- Can we commit to an A/B test that toggles routing policy per-tenant for 2 weeks? Who owns the experiment infra and dashboard?
- For Dedicated, do we default KV cache ON for commit tiers or keep OFF behind opt-in? What's the safety rollback?
- Who can own the Private onboarding checklist and the runbook for KMS rotation (customer-facing doc)?

Hypotheses / trade-offs to call out:
- Enabling KV cache by default for committed Dedicated customers will lower their unit costs noticeably but might increase memory pressure and complicate autoscaling thresholds — need a footprint cap.
- Routing per-tenant experiments give clearer signals than region-level toggles, but require more tagging and quota plumbing.

Data / quick numbers to have ready:
- p95 delta when pinned to latency-tier (hosted nvlink): -110ms, cost +0.9c/token (from INF-1278 perf run)
- Observed token reduction from KV cache proto: 12–18% on top 30% of traffic (internal trace set)
- Current Dedicated pool headroom: ~24% usable before adding GPUs (see capacity sheet link in INF-1278)

Draft experiment plan (for discussion):
- Experiment: routing A/B for 7–14 days, sample: 10% of tenants by usage band (low/high), metrics: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, model fallback count.
- Infra owner: Kiran to confirm. Metric owner: Maya (product analytics) to own dashboard.
- Rollback: immediate revert to region default if errors >0.5% or latency regresses >10%.

KV cache rollout options (trade space):
A) Opt-in via console toggle (safe, slower adoption)
B) Default ON for dedicated-reserved customers + memory cap (aggressive, higher org value)
C) Default OFF but enable via autosuggest from Optimize (balanced)

Action items I want to leave with (assign tentative owners in meeting):
- (Kiran) Confirm infra changes needed for per-tenant routing flags and estimate engineer-days (due: 2026-03-19).
- (Maya) Create A/B dashboard template with p95/cost/error, add to shared dashboard (due: 2026-03-17).
- (Ashley) Draft Dedicated console UX for KV toggle + tooltip + default state copy (due: 2026-03-18).
- (Kiran or designate) Take ownership of Private onboarding checklist: collate KMS, network, audit items and post to Confluence (due: 2026-03-22).
- (All) Quick sync in 1 week to review experiment readiness (timebox 15m).

Notes-to-self / running questions to bring up in 1:1 if we have time:
- Should we push Optimize to proactively recommend KV cache for customers with >5 prompt calls per minute? Risk: noisy heuristics.
- Is there a cheap canary (synthetic traces) that captures the latency differences for pinned pools without using real customer traffic?
- Check whether Dedicated autoscaler can react to memory pressure from KV at 30s granularity.

Slack / links to pull into the meeting:
- #eng-routing thread (Mar 3rd): thread about routing policy variants.
- GH PR runtime#482 — KV cache proto notes.
- INF-1278 JIRA — routing perf runs + capacity sheet.
- Confluence draft: onboarding checklist (link in linked_artifacts).

Tone + ask for the meeting:
- I want a clear owner for infra + metrics so we can run a tight A/B and get a decision before end of sprint.
- Preference: default ON for Dedicated reserved customers if we can limit KV footprint and set a safe memory cap; otherwise opt-in with Optimize nudge.

Possible follow-ups (post-meeting):
- Share short note w/ decisions + owners in #prod-eng and tag SRE for autoscaling check.
- If KV default decision is YES: schedule a short cross-team implementation plan (runtime, console, billing, SRE).

Quick personal prep checklist (do before 1:1):
- Pull latest p95 numbers from INF-1278 and paste into the doc (done).
- DM Kiran to confirm 15–30m block for the A/B infra discussion (pending).
- Draft console copy for toggle — bring screenshots or a tiny Figma link.

End of scratchpad — will tidy and post decisions after the 1:1.

——
Small informal notes (scratch):
- If Kiran mentions staffing, flag that we may need 1-2 sprints of focused work to finish KV autoscaling and routing flags.
- Keep the ask narrow: decision on experiment and owner, not full implementation plan.
